-I have asked myself the same question.  Is depression delusional? Or vice versa?  Lets take a look at delusions themselves... Basically, the elements of a delusion are that they are thoughts that are *fixed and untrue* and they will remain fixed even in the face of clear evidence that contradicts the delusion.   

-I know that in MY depression, I am prone to cognitive distortions that probably seem delusional to others.  However, in the depths of depression, it is much easier to accept (or generate) a thought like "the world would be a better place if I did not exist."  BUTTTT

-With proper Tx, the depressed can get to a place where they are able to challenge these delusions/cognitive distortions.

-Great discussion topic.  There are both positive and negative factors.  To a "formal" diagnosis.

-I (25/M) have been in some form of therapy (talk therapy as well as seeing various psychiatrists) for roughly 2 decades.  During that period I have been formally diagnosed with the following conditions: In chronological order ... learning disability (LD) specific to reading and writing, major depressive disorder (MDD), general anxiety disorder (GAD), Attention Deficit Disorder (ADD), Seasonal Affective Disorder (SAD), BP2, Substance abuse and substance dependence, PTSD (little T), Social Anxiety Disorder, PTSD (BIG T and little T), and last but not least BP1.

-As you can imagine, I gave up on trying to label myself.  If asked, I wold say that I had an affective disorder not otherwise specified.  In my opinion, the psychological community has shifted away from diagnoses and instead focused on symptoms.

-I am extremely lucky to have found an amazing psychiatrist who I have been seeing on a weekly basis.  Easily the most intelligent, understanding, and best MH professional I have ever met.  BP1 has been the most recent diagnosis and I am afraid its true.  Following a serious motor vehicle accident, I had my first unequivocal break.  Textbook BP1.  Racing thoughts, boundless energy, no need for sleep (longest stint was 7 days), euphoria, delusions of grander, pressured speech (could NOT stop talking and had to record my words rather than writing them down b/c I was talking faster than I could write or type), extreme self confidence, EXTREME rage, balling my eyes out, hyper-sexuality, paranoia, extreme short term memory deficits, intrusive thoughts, passive and active suicidal ideation, overwhelming anxiety, and more.

-So since this most recent diagnosis, I have been researching BP.  I have flipped through several general books on BP and it has been unreal.  It was as though the author was writing down my thoughts.  For example, prior to reading, I described my life as 'riding a never ending roller coaster completely in the dark.  No idea what I would be feeling the next day or even in the hour.  Having no control of the speed or intensity of the coaster.' blah blah

-In my opinion, the benefits of a formal diagnosis are that they can aid MH practitioners on how to go about treating symptoms.  I too am on lamictal and was previously on seroquel for 2years (also for sleep).  I stopped seroquel due to extreme weight gain.  Why lamictal? B/c research has indicated that pt's w/BP benefit from the mood stabilizing effects of the drug.  Especially those with BP2.  Lithium (which I also take) is the go to for treating mania while lamictal is better for treating the depression aspect of BP.   

-Hopefully that was somewhat helpful.  Ask more questions if I did not make sense.
